attachments.origin_landmark: inner surface of the ischial tuberosity and ischiopubic ramus
attachments.insertion_landmark: crus of the penis or clitoris

innervation.root_levels: S2-S4 (deep perineal branch of the pudendal nerve)

actions: compresses the crus, forcing blood distally and maintaining erection

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Its action is venous occlusion, not arterial inflow -- it maintains rather than initiates erection.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Palpation-guided (or, in at least one published case, ultrasound-assisted) injection into each ischiocavernosus muscle at the root of the penis/perineum, lateral to the midline raphe, overlying the crus.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Superficial perineal pouch, overlying the crus of the penis/clitoris; more superficial than the deep perineal pouch muscles.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Palpated as a firm band running from the ischial tuberosity/ramus toward the base of the penis, most prominent on a Valsalva-type perineal contraction.
structures_at_risk: crus of the penis/clitoris, directly deep to the muscle -- the vascular structure the injection is intended to relax around, not damage
pudendal neurovascular bundle, running nearby in the ischioanal fossa
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A real, if niche, injection target: botulinum toxin into the ischiocavernosus muscles (alongside the root of the penis) improved intravaginal ejaculation latency time more than injection at either of two other tested sites in a small comparative study of premature ejaculation (75 U abobotulinumtoxinA/side), and a single case report used ultrasound-assisted bilateral injection to reduce muscle tone and prevent recurrence of low-flow priapism by improving venous drainage. Both are genuine but small/early-stage evidence, not an established standard technique.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Elshahid AR, Taher AOA, Nouh AH (2024) Urologia 91(4):824-829, doi:10.1177/03915603241265825 -- comparative injection-site study for premature ejaculation, including bilateral ischiocavernosus injection (PubMed); Reichel G, Stenner A (2018) Urologe A 57(1):40-43, doi:10.1007/s00120-017-0534-x -- case report of ultrasound-assisted bilateral ischiocavernosus botulinum toxin injection for recurrent low-flow priapism (PubMed)
